tests.title: Customer search by Member ID returns the selected customer
tests.goal: A CRM user can locate one existing customer by an exact Member ID.
preconditions: The staging Storeberry Flower admin account is configured in local .env.
At least one customer with a unique Member ID is available in staging.
data: The Member ID of the selected staging customer; do not copy customer details into reports.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM as the Storeberry Flower admin.
Open Customers > Customers.
Select one existing customer and note its Member ID privately.
Enter that exact Member ID in the customer search field and run the search.

expected.text: The customer count is 1 and one matching customer row is shown.
The search result corresponds to the selected customer; no personal customer details are included in the test report.

notes: Picked the 5th customer on page 1 at runtime; Member ID search -> No. of Customer: 1, the only row is that Member ID.

tests.title: Customer Remark search filters the directory
tests.goal: A CRM user can use the separate Remark search field to filter the customer directory.
preconditions: The staging Storeberry Flower admin account is configured in local .env.
data: A unique search term that does not occur in any customer remark.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM as the Storeberry Flower admin.
Open Customers > Customers.
Enter the unique no-match term in the Remark search field and run the search.

expected.text: The customer count is 0 and no customer rows are shown.

notes: Unique no-match term in Search by Remark -> No. of Customer: 0, no rows.

tests.title: Exact order-number search returns the matching order
tests.goal: A CRM user can locate one order by its exact order number.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.
data: Order number of an existing staging order; keep it out of reports.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM.
Open Orders and choose a date range that includes an existing order.
Select an order from the list and note its order number.
Enter that exact number in Order No. and run the search.

expected.text: The result count is 1 and the single row shows the selected order number.
Customer names, contact details, and order contents are not copied into reports.

notes: Picked the 6th order of Last 12 Months; Order No. search -> No. of Order: 1, only that order number shown.

tests.title: Order status tabs show only matching orders
tests.goal: Each order status view limits the list to the selected status.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Orders.
Review All orders, then select Pending payment, Payment review, Payment rejected, Processing, Complete, Canceled, Refunded, Refund order, and Exchanged one at a time.

expected.text: For each selected status, every visible row has that status label.
The All orders view can contain multiple statuses, and an empty status view shows no rows.
Counts are taken from the current page and are not hard-coded.

notes: Each status tab (Pending payment, Payment review, Payment rejected, Processing, Complete, Canceled, Refunded, Refund order) shows only its own status label on page 1 (Processing/Complete also include their (Exchange Order) rows); All orders mixes statuses. Exchanged is a flag (exchanged_order=1), not a status: rows keep Processing/Complete and their detail shows Exchanged: n (checked 3). No empty tab today.

tests.title: Order date presets and custom range constrain results
tests.goal: A CRM user can restrict orders to a selected creation-date range.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.
data: A valid custom start date and end date.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Orders.
Select Last 3 Months, Last 6 Months, and Last 12 Months in turn.
Choose Custom and enter a valid start and end date.

expected.text: The selected date range is shown after each selection.
Every visible order creation date is within the chosen range.
The count updates with the range and is not a fixed number.

notes: Last 3/6/12 Months start at today minus 3/6/12 months (oldest order on the last page is on that start date); custom 2026-10-01..2026-10-15 -> 32 orders, all created inside the range; inputs keep the dates.

tests.title: Product name or SKU search finds matching orders
tests.goal: A CRM user can find orders containing a selected product by its name or SKU.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.
data: Product name or SKU from an existing staging order; do not include customer details.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Orders.
Choose an existing order with a product line and note the product name or SKU privately.
Enter the product name or SKU in Product Name / SKU and run the search.

expected.text: The result includes the order containing the selected product.
The result count reflects the matching orders and no customer details are included in reports.

notes: Product name taken from an order line at runtime (鞋C) -> 12 orders, incl. the picked one; all 12 contain 鞋C (10 checked in detail because delivered/POS rows list no items). Searching the full line text "name (option)" returns 0: search matches the product name only.

tests.title: Product ID search returns the selected catalog item
tests.goal: A CRM user can locate an active product by its unique product ID.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.
data: Product ID of a currently active staging product.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Products.
Select an active product and note its Product ID.
Enter the ID in Product ID, Name, Option, SKU, Barcode and run the search.

expected.text: The result count is 1 and the row shows the selected Product ID and product name.
The selected product remains active and unchanged.

notes: Product ID of the 10th active product -> No. of Product: 1, same ID and name, still Launched.

tests.title: Package view contains only package products
tests.goal: The Package product view displays records classified as packages.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Products.
Select Package.
Review the listed product types across the result pages.

expected.text: Every listed row has Product Type Package.
The displayed product count matches the filtered package result set and is not hard-coded.

notes: Package(8) view -> 8 rows, all Product Type Package; count matches the tab.

tests.title: On-sale view contains products with active discounts
tests.goal: The On Sale Products view contains only products currently marked on sale.
preconditions: Dedicated Storeberry Flower staging admin account is configured in local .env.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Products.
Select On Sale Products.
Review the visible product prices and promotion/discount indicators.

expected.text: The view is filtered to its on-sale product set.
Each visible result has an on-sale price or active promotion/discount indicator.
The count changes with the current data and is not hard-coded.

notes: On Sale Products (13) -> 13 rows; each has at least one variant with Final Price below Original Price (all 13 checked); a regular product has Final = Original. The Promotions column is not a sale indicator: every product shows the whole-basket promo "All Basket & member Free Shipping".

tests.title: Inventory search locates stock by SKU or barcode
tests.goal: A CRM user can locate a product or variant in inventory using its SKU or barcode.
preconditions: An active inventory item with a SKU or barcode is available.
data: SKU or barcode of an existing staging item; do not include personal data.

steps.text: Sign in to the staging CRM and open Inventory.
Select an existing product variant and note its SKU or barcode privately.
Search by that exact SKU or barcode.

expected.text: The matching product or variant appears in the results.
The row shows the corresponding inventory quantities and platform status.

notes: Inventory variants view, SKU picked from a variant row -> No. of variants: 1, same product, variant, SKU, Available/Stock qty and Launched status. Barcode not tried.
